correctness.rationale: All even n>=4: parity across 2j-vertex column cuts excludes exactly one twisted seam; every perfect matching belongs to one of two forced-edge cones. Exact intersection is the middle odd-length open ladder perfect-matching complex, proved by the outer-column extension/replacement lemma. Odd open-ladder complexes are contractible by a two-cone recurrence and finite-CW homotopy-pushout gluing. The resulting union is contractible. The standard-library verification independently checks all facet decompositions at n=4,6,8,10,12 and exhaustive free-face collapses at n=4,6,8,10; finite checks do not establish the universal theorem.

value.rationale: A single naturally distinguished antipodal edge deletion changes a known, noncontractible two-sphere wedge perfect-matching complex to a point for infinitely many even widths. The parity-forced seam states and exact contractible intersection explain the boundary sensitivity structurally, beyond merely repeating known odd open-ladder contractibility or conducting finite enumeration.
